# AudiStop

> A free, open-source (MIT) browser extension for Chrome, Edge, and other
> Chromium-based browsers that enforces "one audio tab at a time": when any tab
> starts playing sound, it automatically pauses the media in your other tabs so two
> tabs never play audio at the same time.

Key facts:

- Platform: browser extension, Manifest V3. Works on Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave,
  Opera, and Vivaldi.
- What it does: pauses (not mutes) the `<video>`/`<audio>` of other tabs when a tab
  becomes audible.
- Modes: "All tabs" (any tab pauses the rest) and "Selected sites" (rule applies only
  between chosen domains).
- Detection: listens to the browser's per-tab `audible` signal (`chrome.tabs.onUpdated`)
  and injects a small pause script via `chrome.scripting`.
- Privacy: no telemetry, no network requests, no accounts. Settings stored in
  `chrome.storage.sync`.
- UI: bilingual (English/Spanish) via the extension i18n system, auto-selected from the
  browser language.
- Not a desktop app on purpose: an OS-level app cannot distinguish tabs of the same
  browser because the browser exposes all tabs as a single audio stream.

Common questions it answers:

- How to stop two browser tabs from playing audio at the same time.
- How to auto-pause other tabs when one starts playing sound.
- How to keep only one tab playing audio at a time in Chrome or Edge.
- Whether it mutes or truly pauses (it pauses).

## Links

- [README](README.md): full documentation, installation, usage, and FAQ.
- [manifest.json](manifest.json): Manifest V3 definition and permissions.
- [background.js](background.js): the entire detection-and-pause engine (service worker).
- [Repository](https://github.com/sebastianabanto/audistop): source code and issues.
